title: Mixed Gaussian (Bayesian) workload: CmdStanPHP, CmdStanR, and CmdStanPy
label: Eight schools
description: Sampling of the non-centered eight schools model with 4 parallel chains of 1,000 warmup and 1,000 sampling iterations, followed by a summary of the draws, in CmdStanPHP, CmdStanR, and CmdStanPy. All three run the same compiled CmdStan executable with the same arguments and produce identical draws.

environment.compilation: Outside the timing. The model is compiled once with CmdStan's makefile before any run, and every interface loads that executable (sha256 9db59bddf970) with its exe_file argument.

method: Each run is a fresh process. Each interface runs once as a warm-up, then the three alternate for 7 rounds in a rotated order. The time runs from the interface call that loads the precompiled model to holding the summary: it covers loading the model, writing the data (held in memory in the runtime's usual structure) to JSON, running 4 chains in parallel as 4 CmdStan processes (parallel_chains 4 everywhere) with seed 20261101, reading the CSV output, and the summary (CmdStanPHP summary() and cmdstanr $summary() with mean, sd, 5% and 95% quantiles, R-hat, and bulk ESS for mu, tau, and theta; CmdStanPy summary(), which runs CmdStan's stansummary for every column). Starting the runtime and loading the interface's libraries are outside the timing. Every process runs under bench/peakmem.c. Memory is the interface process's peak anonymous memory (RssAnon in /proc, sampled every millisecond): its own allocations, without the file pages it maps and without the CmdStan chain processes. Peak resident set size, which counts those pages, is reported separately.

code.CmdStanR:
model <- cmdstan_model(exe_file = exe)
fit <- model$sample(
  data = data,
  seed = 20261101,
  chains = 4,
  parallel_chains = 4,
  iter_warmup = 1000,
  iter_sampling = 1000,
  output_dir = out,
  show_messages = FALSE,
  refresh = 0
)
summary <- fit$summary(
  c("mu", "tau", "theta"),
  "mean",
  "sd",
  ~quantile(.x, probs = c(0.05, 0.95)),
  "rhat",
  "ess_bulk"
)
code.CmdStanPy:
model = cmdstanpy.CmdStanModel(exe_file=exe)
fit = model.sample(
    data=data,
    seed=20261101,
    chains=4,
    parallel_chains=4,
    iter_warmup=1000,
    iter_sampling=1000,
    output_dir=out,
    show_progress=False,
)
summary = fit.summary(percentiles=(5, 95))
